Topic: The Magic of Light: Principles of Holography and Diffraction

Target audience: University Undergraduate Physics Students

Section: section_1 — Prerequisite: The Wave Nature of Light

Lecture lines:
Light acts as an electromagnetic wave.
Waves possess both amplitude and phase.
Superposition creates interference patterns.
Constructive interference adds peak to peak.
Destructive interference cancels peaks out.

Planned animations:
Create a central light source emitting wave ripples.
Fade in a barrier showing wave propagation patterns.
Highlight interference fringes appearing on a screen.
Color the light source to indicate coherent wave frequency.
Morph ripples into a standard wavefront representation.

Section: section_2 — Understanding Diffraction

Lecture lines:
Diffraction is waves bending around obstacles.
Objects transform waves into spatial patterns.
Fourier transforms map these spatial frequencies.

Planned animations:
Show two beams meeting at a point.
Animate interference pattern expansion with #FF00FF light.
Show barrier edges causing wave bending animations.
Display intensity plot update with bright #00FFFF lines.
Label the diffraction angle with #FFFFFF math text.

Section: section_3 — The Holography Mechanism: Recording

Lecture lines:
Photographs capture only light intensity.
Holography records the interference pattern.
Reference beams provide constant phase.
Object beams reflect off the subject.
Interference freezes phase data on film.

Planned animations:
Illustrate object beam and reference beam geometry.
Animate beam convergence on a photographic plate.
Show interference fringe pattern forming on the plate.

Section: section_4 — The Holography Mechanism: Reconstruction

Lecture lines:
Reconstruction uses the reference beam.
The hologram acts like a key.
Original wavefronts emerge from diffraction.
This reconstructs the 3D volume.
Viewing angles shift perspective accurately.

Planned animations:
Show reference beam striking the recorded hologram.
Animate reconstruction of the virtual object wave.
Display the reconstructed image appearing behind the hologram.

Section: section_5 — Synthesis and Applications

Lecture lines:
Fourier optics explain holographic storage.
We map 3D space to 2D.
Technology secures credit card data.

Planned animations:
Display 3D scanning concept using hologram data.
Show secure authentication via holographic key systems.
Visualize data storage in holographic optical materials.

class TeachingScene(Scene):
    def setup_layout(self, title_text, lecture_lines):
        # BASE
        self.camera.background_color = "#000000"
        self.title = Text(title_text, font_size=28, color=WHITE).to_edge(UP)
        self.add(self.title)

        # Left-side lecture content (bullets with "-")
        lecture_texts = [Text(line, font_size=22, color=WHITE) for line in lecture_lines]
        self.lecture = VGroup(*lecture_texts).arrange(DOWN, aligned_edge=LEFT).scale(0.8)
        self.lecture.to_edge(LEFT, buff=0.2)
        self.add(self.lecture)

        # Define fine-grained animation grid (4x4 grid on right side)
        self.grid = {}
        rows = ["A", "B", "C", "D", "E", "F"]  # Top to bottom
        cols = ["1", "2", "3", "4", "5", "6"]  # Left to right

        for i, row in enumerate(rows):
            for j, col in enumerate(cols):
                x = 0.5 + j * 1
                y = 2.2 - i * 1
                self.grid[f"{row}{col}"] = np.array([x, y, 0])

    def place_at_grid(self, mobject, grid_pos, scale_factor=1.0):
        mobject.scale(scale_factor)
        mobject.move_to(self.grid[grid_pos])
        return mobject

        tl_pos = self.grid[top_left]
        br_pos = self.grid[bottom_right]
        
        # Calculate center of the area
        center_x = (tl_pos[0] + br_pos[0]) / 2
        center_y = (tl_pos[1] + br_pos[1]) / 2
        center = np.array([center_x, center_y, 0])
        
        mobject.scale(scale_factor)
        mobject.move_to(center)
        return mobject
